pr_title: IJSUnmarshalledObjectReference for unmarshalled JS interop calls on JavaScript objects. Fixes #25208
pr_body:
#### Description

Added `IJSUnmarshalledObjectReference`, allowing high-performance JS interop calls on Blazor WebAssembly.

#### Customer Impact

Component vendors may utilize unmarshalled JS interop calls for improved performance.

#### Regression?

No.

#### Risk

Little risk - this is an area that is well tested.

Addresses #25208

issue_context.title: Support unmarshalled calls to JSObjectReference
issue_context.body: We plan to do this in RC2. It's a pretty small bit of work to complete the new JSObjectReference feature set.
comments: This is actually being done by @MackinnonBuck so I'm transferring the assignment to him.

review_comments:
Ah, unless I'm missing something, I think we made a mistake in a previous recent change here. Sorry for not spotting this during code review before. Looks like the confusion was [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/24640/files#r469861702).

It appears that https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/24640/files#diff-514554bd1120b4f06b0ba9fee70c3792 made a breaking change to this public type which we didn't plan for. The various public overloads of `InvokeUnmarshalled` were all removed and replaced by an explicit interface implementation.

I don't think there's any reason we should want to introduce a breaking change for those. When RC1 ships, we're likely to get a few confused customers asking what's going on as various 3rd-party libraries will break. We can give them a workaround for RC1 (cast to `IJSUnmarshalledRuntime`).

Can we please put back the same public `InvokeUnmarshalled` methods onto this type to restore compatibility with 3.2? It can still implement `IJSUnmarshalledRuntime` but those implementations should be regular public methods.
Ah, good catch. I've made these public again.
I thought it made sense that `IJSInProcessObjectReference`s should be able to be disposed synchronously.
Well done for remembering to change this!

@SteveSandersonMS and I discussed this change. We decided it was the best way to avoid giving IVT access to `M.A.Components.WebAssembly`. It follows a similar pattern as `JSRuntime`, which is also a public type. `JSObjectReference` is less visible in `M.JSInterop.Implementation`, and its constructor is `protected internal`, so customers aren't likely to use it by accident. Furthermore, [this](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/25548/files#diff-2ba950045b5f06e6358c8cd052780120R9-R11) prevents developers from accidentally doing something like `JSRuntime.InvokeAsync<JSObjectReference>()`.
@SteveSandersonMS and I discussed this offline - I am going to file a separate issue for this since it's not crucial it gets implemented right now.
